description: The tube above the bench coughs and drops a brass canister into the tray. Inside, on Counting-House paper, is a bill: back rent on No. 9 Sprocket Row, 15 Crowns, payable at the Counting-House window. Underneath, in smaller writing: "The last tenant left owing. It is not your fault, but it is now your workshop. I only run the bills. Sorry. Pip Tumbler." The Arrears dial under your portrait twitches awake and settles at 0.

options.label: Spike the bill and pay it at the Counting-House window when you have the Crowns.

success.text: You push the bill onto the spike above the vice, where it can watch you work. Fifteen Crowns counted through the Counting-House window will take it down again. Until then it stays where it is, and so, you suspect, does Pip's apology.

options.label: Write back offering to work some of it off at the bench.

success.text: The canister comes back within the hour holding a carriage clock that has not struck since anyone can remember, and a note: "A Counting-House clerk's. If it strikes, I can take 10 off." You take the back off, find a hairspring wound round itself like a nervous cat, and coax it straight. At six o'clock the clock strikes seven. The clerk, Pip reports, accepts this as close enough. You owe 5 Crowns.

failure.text: Pip sends down a Counting-House clerk's carriage clock. You return it in two parcels, one of them mostly spring. The reply is polite and brief: the bill stands at 15 Crowns, and the clerk has asked Pip for your name, twice. The Arrears dial ticks up two marks.
